from.place: Final paragraph of def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility: the full class of complexes with finitely many nonzero constructible cohomology sheaves is asserted to be triangulated.

title: Bounded constructible pro-etale complexes form a triangulated subcategory
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring, let $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ be the derived category of sheaves of $\Lambda_Y$-modules on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and for $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ and $i\in\mathbf Z$ let $\mathcal H^i(K)$ be its $i$-th cohomology sheaf [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Let $P$ be the property of $K$: $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for all but finitely many $i$, and every $\mathcal H^i(K)$ is a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. Then $P$ is closed under isomorphisms and defines a full triangulated subcategory of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]: $0$ satisfies $P$; $K$ satisfies $P$ if and only if $K[n]$ does, for every $n\in\mathbf Z$; and for every distinguished triangle $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$ with $K$ and $M$ satisfying $P$, also $L$ satisfies $P$.

source.place: Pro-etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 61.27.3 (Tag 09AL, label lemma-compare-constructible-derived), from Lemma 61.27.2 (Tag 09B5, label lemma-constructible-serre: constructible sheaves form a weak Serre subcategory) and Derived Categories, Section 13.17 (Tag 06UP), Lemma Tag 06UQ (label lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory, bounded version); also literature/bhatt-scholze-pro-etale-topology_arXiv-1309.1198.pdf, Definition 1.1 (3)

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_Y)$ on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, with universe sizes chosen as in the category of module sheaves. It is abelian. Its derived category is precisely $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$, and the functors $H^i$ of $D(\mathcal A)$ are the sheaves $\mathcal H^i$ appearing in the statement. Let $\mathcal B$ be the full subcategory of the globally constructible sheaves. These are choices of the category and its full subcategory, without changing the constructibility convention. The zero sheaf is locally constant with zero stalks on the single stratum $Y$; transporting the finite partition and its local trivializations through an isomorphism shows that $\mathcal B$ is strictly full. Also $\Lambda$ is Noetherian: an ascending chain of ideals is an ascending chain of subsets of its finite underlying set and stabilizes.

source.place: Proof of Tag 09AL, label lemma-compare-constructible-derived: identify the ambient module category and the constructible cohomology class.

proof.text:
For every scheme map $f:X\to Y$, [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] identifies the specified $c^f_\Lambda$ with an isomorphism. Thus [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] supplies the exact module inverse image; after forgetting the module action it is the abelian inverse image. For a weakly etale $j:U\to X$, [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction] identifies $j^*$ with localized restriction. Applying [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-stalk] to the underlying abelian sheaf gives
$$(F|_U)_{\bar u}\cong F_{j\bar u}.$$
This stalk isomorphism is used below only for finiteness of underlying sets, so no scalar comparison beyond these identifications is required.

source.place: Tags 03CE (lemma-localize-given-products), 05V1 (lemma-point-morphism-sites), specialized to the pro-etale site; coefficient map as in proetale.tex 09A5.

proof.text: Every geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ lifts to a member of any pro-etale covering $\{U_j\to X\}$. Indeed, base change along $\bar x$ gives a covering $\{U_j\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\}$ by the covering-preserving base-change functor of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Joint surjectivity in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] gives a point $v$ of some fibre. This fibre is weakly etale over $\Omega$ by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change]. Restricting to an affine neighbourhood of $v$ preserves weakly etaleness by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-source-locality]. There, [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field] makes $\kappa(v)/\Omega$ separable algebraic. Since $\Omega$ is algebraically closed this extension is $\Omega$ itself. Its point map gives a lift $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U_j$ over $X$. The same argument applies to coverings of every stratum.

source.place: Definition of covering families; more-algebra.tex Tag 092Q (lemma-absolutely-flat-over-field) for the fibre residue fields.

proof.text: On any scheme $T$, a locally constant sheaf $F$ has finite geometric stalks if and only if it admits finite constant local models. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-constant-restriction] and [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], the localized constant module models in the definition are constant module sheaves on the members’ own pro-etale sites. Use the covering and module models $M_j$ of [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. If $U_j$ is nonempty, choose a point and an algebraic closure of its residue field, obtaining a geometric point $\bar u$ as in [def-weil-geometric-point]. Step 2 and [lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk] identify $M_j\cong(F|_{U_j})_{\bar u}\cong F_{j\bar u}$, so finite stalks imply $M_j$ is finite. Empty members may be discarded. Conversely, for an arbitrary geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$, step 3 gives a lift to some $U_j$. The same two stalk isomorphisms identify $F_{\bar t}$ with that finite $M_j$. This proves finiteness at every geometric point, rather than just at a chosen point of each member.

source.place: Tag 099Y (lemma-compare-locally-constant): constant local models; geometric stalk comparison as in Tag 0993 (lemma-classical-point).

proof.text: For any scheme map $f:X\to T$, inverse image preserves locally constant sheaves with finite stalks. Choose finite local models $M_j$ for $F$ by step 4. The hypotheses of [lem-exc-proetale-pullback-locally-constant] hold: the ring is finite, the pullback uses its specified canonical constant-ring map, and the local models are finite modules. Its displayed comparison gives finite constant models for $f^*F$ on the base-changed covering $\{X\times_TU_j\to X\}$. Step 4 then gives finite stalks at every geometric point of $X$. In particular this uses preservation of the same finite module values, rather than only preservation of local constancy.

source.place: Tag 03D8 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules); constant-model specialization of Tags 093I and 093R, with localization from sites.tex Tag 03CE.

proof.text: For $F,G\in\mathcal B$, choose the two finite stratifications in [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-stratification-intersection] to obtain their common finite stratification by fibre products. Each refined stratum maps to an old stratum through the corresponding projection. Composition of module inverse images [lem-pur-proetale-module-pullback-composition] identifies restriction from $Y$ with this successive pullback. Step 5 therefore shows that both restricted sheaves are locally constant with finite stalks on every refined stratum.

source.place: Tag 03RZ (lemma-constructible-abelian), common finite partition argument, carried out on the given global partitions.

proof.text: For a morphism $u:F\to G$ in $\mathcal B$, use the common stratification from step 6. By step 4 its two restricted sheaves have finite constant models, whose finite underlying sets generate them as $\Lambda$-modules. Thus they are locally constant of finite type. The module inverse image is exact by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], so restriction of $\ker u$ and $\operatorname{coker}u$ is the kernel and cokernel of the restricted morphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-derived-serre] on the small pro-etale site of each stratum, with $B=\Lambda$, Noetherian by step 1. The two resulting sheaves are locally constant of finite type. Each finitely generated local model is a quotient of $\Lambda^r$ for some finite $r$, hence finite as a set. Step 4 gives finite stalks at every geometric point. The same finite stratification therefore witnesses constructibility of both sheaves. For $0\to F\to E\to G\to0$, use the common finite stratification of the outside terms; exact restriction and the extension clause of the same lemma give locally constant finite-type restrictions of $E$. Their models and all geometric stalks are finite by the preceding argument. Thus $E$ is constructible. Together with step 1, this supplies all weak-Serre hypotheses for the global finite-stratification convention [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf].

source.place: Tag 093U, lemma-kernel-finite-locally-constant (3), stratumwise; global finite-partition form of proetale.tex Tag 09B5, lemma-constructible-serre.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-cohomology-in-weak-serre-subcategory] to $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$. Step 1 supplies the abelian category and its derived cohomology, and steps 1 and 7 supply every closure hypothesis. The bounded version of that lemma gives a strictly full triangulated subcategory $D_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal A)\cap D^b(\mathcal A)$ of $D(\mathcal A)$ with its inherited shifts and distinguished triangles.

source.place: Tag 06UQ, label lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory, including its bounded versions; this is the general result used in the proof of Tag 09AL.

proof.text: By the definition of $D^b(\mathcal A)$, membership means that only finitely many $H^i$ are nonzero. By the identification in step 1, membership in $D_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal A)$ means exactly that every $\mathcal H^i$ is constructible. Thus the property of the subcategory in step 8 is exactly $P$. Strict fullness gives invariance under isomorphisms; the inherited triangulated structure gives zero, all shifts, and closure of the middle vertex of a distinguished triangle whose outside vertices satisfy $P$. Applying shift closure first to $[n]$ and then to $[-n]$, whose composite is isomorphic to the identity, gives the claimed if and only if for shifts.

source.place: Tag 06UQ, label lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory; Section Tag 06UP, label section-triangulated-sub, definition of the bounded class.
